ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Srinivasa Ramanujan — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: New patient with four weeks of evening fevers and night sweats, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain, in a 29-year-old mathematician from Tamil Nadu who came to a research fellowship here three years ago

text.paragraph: New patient with four weeks of evening fevers and night sweats, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain, in a 29-year-old mathematician from Tamil Nadu who came to a research fellowship here three years ago [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: He is afraid he has tuberculosis and wants to know what is wrong. [S]
He wants to keep working on his mathematics while he is treated. [S]
He wants any food and medicine advice to fit his diet and his tradition. [S]
He feels alone here and misses his family. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887 in his grandmother's house in Erode, in what is now Tamil Nadu, and grew up in Kumbakonam. His father, Kuppuswamy Srinivasa, was a clerk in a cloth merchant's shop, and his mother, Komalatammal, sang devotional songs; the family was Brahmin and poor. [D]

He had no family name in the Western sense. In Tamil usage the father's given name comes first as an initial or prefix, so "Srinivasa" is his father's name and "Ramanujan" is his own given name, the name by which he was known and addressed. [D]
He had smallpox in December 1889, fell ill after about three months at a college in Madras in 1906, and had a serious illness in 1908 followed by an operation in 1909 and a long recovery. [D]
He had two episodes of dysentery in India, about eleven and eight years before his illness in England. [D]

He married Janaki in July 1909, worked as a clerk at the Madras Port Trust from March 1912, wrote to G. H. Hardy at Cambridge in January 1913, sailed for England in March 1914, and moved into rooms at Trinity College, Cambridge, at the end of April 1914. [D]

An orthodox Brahmin, he was a strict vegetarian. He had trouble with his diet from the start in England; the war that began a few months after his arrival made the foods he needed harder to get, and he cooked for himself, sometimes only once a day or every other day. [D]

text.paragraph: 9 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

list.item: Mathematician holding a research fellowship at a university here; came from Tamil Nadu three years ago; before that a clerk in a port office while he worked on mathematics on his own; works long hours, often through the night [S]
Lives alone in a college room with a small kitchen; married, and his wife lives with his parents in India; calls home rarely and letters are slow; few friends here who share his language or food [S]

Strict lacto-vegetarian by his tradition: rice, lentils and other pulses, vegetables, fruit, milk, curd and ghee; no meat, fish or eggs; cooks for himself, prefers food prepared by himself or within his tradition, and in recent weeks has cooked only once a day or less; finds few of his foods in local shops [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: never, by his tradition. No drug use [S]
Hindu; prays daily; his faith and his mathematics matter most to him [S]
Stipend from his fellowship; student health insurance; no car; walks everywhere [S]
Prefers to be addressed as Mr. Ramanujan; explains that Srinivasa is his father's name and that he has no family name [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Quiet and courteous, thoughtful, with soft speech and some slowing; mood low and worried; affect constricted but brightens when he talks about his work; thought clear and logical; no thoughts of self-harm; PHQ-9 12, GAD-7 9. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

code.displayName: Physical findings of General status Narrative

text.paragraph: Alert and engaged. Independent in daily activities, but tired by afternoon, cooking less, and has missed some seminars in the last two weeks. [S]

Vital signs recorded on 1917-01-12; see the Vital Signs section. Mental status: Quiet and courteous, thoughtful, with soft speech and some slowing; mood low and worried; affect constricted but brightens when he talks about his work; thought clear and logical; no thoughts of self-harm; PHQ-9 12, GAD-7 9. The physical examination is limited to the findings relevant to this synthetic episode. [S]

Structured safety assessment: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent, access to means reviewed: yes. Outpatient care with close follow-up. He has no thoughts of suicide or self-harm now and has had none. Because he is ill, isolated, far from home and screening in the moderate range, his risk factors were reviewed with him privately and a written safety plan was made: his warning signs (not sleeping, not eating, not wanting to see anyone), what helps, who he can call, and the clinic number. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline was given and saved in his phone. Lethal-means counseling: no firearm; medicines dispensed in short supplies. Safety reviewed at every visit. [S]

Infectious diseases consultation at the second visit for fever, weight loss and right upper quadrant pain in a young man from South India with a history of dysentery, to interpret the tuberculosis and amebiasis tests, the imaging, and the choice and order of treatment. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Clinical Practice Guidelines: Diagnosis of Tuberculosis in Adults and Children (2017); DPDx: Amebiasis (laboratory diagnosis, including antibody detection in extraintestinal disease) (2026) [S]

Tuberculosis evaluation before any antibiotic: chest radiograph, three induced sputum samples for acid-fast smear, NAAT and mycobacterial culture, an interferon-gamma release assay, and HIV testing; airborne precautions until three smears are negative. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Official American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Clinical Practice Guidelines: Diagnosis of Tuberculosis in Adults and Children (2017) [S]

Liver and gut evaluation: abdominal ultrasound tomorrow morning, Entamoeba histolytica serology, stool antigen or PCR and microscopy, two sets of blood cultures, liver tests and CRP. Guideline: DPDx: Amebiasis (laboratory diagnosis, including antibody detection in extraintestinal disease) (2026); A Review of the Global Burden, New Diagnostics, and Current Therapeutics for Amebiasis (2018) [S]

Nutrition: vitamin B12, folate, ferritin and 25-hydroxyvitamin D measured; weight at every visit; a dietitian visit to plan meals within his vegetarian diet and his rules. Guideline: Position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics: Vegetarian Diets (2016); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and depression monographs (2026) [S]

Mood and safety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at least monthly while symptoms last; structured safety assessment and a written safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; safety reviewed at every visit; short-term counseling with the university counseling service, at times he chooses. Guideline: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and depression monographs (2026); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024) [S]

Support far from home: the university's international student office and his department's graduate office about leave and deadlines while he is ill; a regular time to call his family; introductions, at his wish, to the local Tamil association and a Hindu temple community with shared meals; a letter for his fellowship about his illness. Guideline: Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]

Acetaminophen for fever and pain, no more than 3 g a day; nothing else until the results are known. Guideline: DPDx: Amebiasis (laboratory diagnosis, including antibody detection in extraintestinal disease) (2026) [S]
Referral to infectious diseases, Priya Raghunathan, MD, ordered 1917-01-12 [S]
